claims: The 25th Amendment was ratified in 1967 following President Kennedy's assassination.
Section 1 of the 25th Amendment states that if the President dies, resigns, or is removed, the Vice President becomes President.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment states that the President nominates a Vice President who takes office upon confirmation by a majority vote in both Houses of Congress.

Section 3 of the 25th Amendment states that the President may declare in writing that they are unable to discharge their duties, making the Vice President the Acting President until they submit a declaration to the contrary.

Section 4 of the 25th Amendment states that the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet (or another body designated by Congress) can declare the President disabled, making the Vice President Acting President.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1973-1974 to appoint Gerald Ford as Vice President after Spiro Agnew's resignation.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1973-1974 for Gerald Ford to become President after Richard Nixon's resignation.
Presidents Reagan, G.W. Bush, and Biden used the 25th Amendment to temporarily transfer power while undergoing surgery or anesthesia.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been officially used.
